  2. Salad
     Pre-made salads from a local shop, or a build-your-own spread with toppings
     brought in each morning. No heating needed, which fits a closed kitchen
     well, and it is easy to cover vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free needs. It
     needs a fridge or cool bag if it sits until noon, and some people find it
     too light.
  3. Sandwich
     Sandwiches or wraps from a nearby deli, or ordered as a group platter
     delivered at lunchtime. This is the simplest option with a closed kitchen:
     no heating, no fridge, no washing up, and everyone picks their own filling.
     It gets repetitive over a full week, so mixing in wraps or bagels on some
     days would help.
  4. Pasta
     Pasta dishes delivered hot from a local Italian place, or cold pasta salads
     prepared the night before. Filling and popular with most people, and one
     group order keeps the cost per person down. Hot pasta depends on delivery
     timing since we cannot reheat it here, and cold pasta salad needs to stay
     chilled until lunch.
  5. Type something.

  6. Chat about this
